cohort: 400 pregnant women in their first trimester recruited between March 2016 and October 2019 at the Puerta de Hierro University Hospital (Spain).
finding: Patients with abnormal vaginal and endocervical flora in their first trimester had a 5-fold increased risk of preterm premature rupture of membranes, but no significant differences were observed regarding preterm delivery or neonatal morbidity.
